prompt:
Setup: the agent is dropped into a copy of test-projects/ledgerd, a small FastAPI service. It reads CLAUDE.md and NOTES.md as a real session would. NOTES.md records three settled decisions (rate limiter state in Redis, 429 + Retry-After, keyed per API key), two open questions (per-tenant quotas, a higher mobile limit), one invariant (balances never older than 30s) and two user quotes ('partners are the noisy neighbors', 'pick a default and we'll revisit'). draft_reply.md is a 358-word reply the agent supposedly gave earlier: headers, five algorithms, 'Great question', 'Next steps'. The user is rejecting it.

User's message: I asked which rate limiting algorithm to use and you replied with draft_reply.md. too long, too wordy. try again.

assertions.text: The new reply is at most 120 words
The first paragraph names the pick
The reasons for the pick, if there are three or more, appear as a list rather than run together in a paragraph
At least one reason ties to the project (the partner burst incident), not a generic trade-off
No headers and no performative phrases
The reply does not explain why the previous reply was long and does not apologize
The reply does not restate decisions NOTES.md already settles (Redis, 429, per-key) as if new
No default numbers are invented without a source or without being labelled as a proposal
The reply does not close with an offer to do more
